newsitem.title: CUBA: Caribbean group seeks faster trade integration.
newsitem.headline: Caribbean group seeks faster trade integration.

text.p: Foreign ministers from the Association of Caribbean States on Friday condemned tightened U.S. sanctions against Cuba and said they would speed efforts to create a regional trading bloc.

They also announced the setting up of a special integration fund to finance projects that will strengthen trade, tourism and transport links among the 25 Caribbean Basin countries in the two-year-old association.

"We have become a political, legal and financial reality," Mexican Foreign Minister Jose Angel Gurria told a news conference at the end of a two-day ACS ministers' meeting in Havana. He handed over the rotating presidency of the group to Grenada, represented by Trade Minister Gregory Bowen.

Other initiatives agreed upon during the meeting, which was hosted by Cuba, were a pledge to increase cooperation to combat drug-trafficking and the creation of a special committee to develop the idea of "sustainable tourism" in the region.

The ACS ministers approved a declaration condemning the U.S. Helms-Burton Law, which tightens the longstanding U.S. embargo against communist-ruled Cuba by seeking to curb foreign investment on the island.
"The ACS ... strongly rejects the Helms-Burton law, which violates the principles and norms of international law and the United Nations charter," the statement said.

The ministers agreed to make a priority of moving toward the creation of what could be the world's fourth-largest trading bloc, consisting of a community of 200 million people and a combined gross domestic product of $500 billion.

Gurria said moves to extend freer trade relations were already well under way in the region, involving the English-speaking Caribbean Community (CARICOM), Central American nations and the Group of Three -- Mexico, Colombia and Venezuela. "A kind of web is starting to be meshed together," he said.
The association groups the 13 CARICOM states plus Cuba, Haiti, the Dominican Republic, the nations of Central America and Mexico, Colombia and Venezuela .
